author: Connor McCrory
title: Inside Celeste Rivas' devastating autopsy as singer D4vd arrested over teen's death - NewsBreak
text:
By Connor McCrory ,
1 hours ago Celeste Abigail Rivas Hernandez, the 14-year-old, whose disappearance and gruesome discovery inside an impounded Tesla belonging to R&B singer D4vd shook the nation, was stabbed multiple times and dismembered, according to a full autopsy report released Wednesday by the Los Angeles County Department of Medical Examiner.
The complete findings, made public April 22, days after D4vd was charged with her murder , confirm for the first time the full, horrifying extent of injuries suffered by the teenage girl whose case drew widespread attention after her remains were found stuffed inside a black body bag in the front trunk of the singer's Tesla at a Los Angeles police impound lot last September.
The report details two deep stab wounds to the torso. One entered the right abdomen and tore through the liver. The second pierced the left chest wall, penetrated the space between the ribs, and fractured the cortical bone of adjacent ribs.

Rivas Hernandez had been reported missing in April 2024, and the autopsy was performed on September 10, 2025. Toxicology testing on liver tissue detected a low level of ethanol, which the medical examiner noted may have resulted from the decomposition process rather than ingestion and was not considered a contributing cause of death.
Tests for methamphetamine and designer opioids returned inconclusive results due to interfering substances.
Chief Medical Examiner Dr. Odey Ukpo said Wednesday the delay had prolonged an already unimaginable ordeal for the teenager's family.
"After several months, I am grateful this information can now be released, not only to the public, but also to the grieving family enduring loss," Ukpo said in a statement . "It is unfathomable they have had to wait this long to learn what happened to their daughter."
Ukpo framed the public release as a matter of community accountability and social justice.
"The transparency of the information contained in our findings and reports is essential for empowering the community to make informed changes to affectively reduce fear and allowing the community to take informed action," he said.
"Making the Department's information publicly available is not just about accountability, it is about social justice and prevention. By ensuring access to this information, we strengthen our ability to learn, to act, and ultimately to prevent the next tragic loss of life."
D4vd, whose legal name is David Burke, was arrested on April 16 and is being held without bail. His attorneys pushed back forcefully on the charges.
"Let us be clear, the actual evidence in this case will show that David Burke did not murder Celeste Rivas Hernandez and he was not the cause of her death," attorneys Blair Berk, Marilyn Bednarski, and Regina Peter said. "David has only been detained under suspicion. We will vigorously defend David's innocence."
LAPD's Robbery Homicide Division is leading the investigation.
